title: Audit log cardinality + volume budget (WIP)
content:
Context
- This is a spreadsheet-style working doc to sanity-check (1) audit event volume, (2) event payload size, and (3) high-cardinality fields that can break dashboards/alerts if mistakenly used as metric labels/dimensions.
- Primary audience: service owners adding events + telemetry/observability (dashboards, SLOs) + exporter (SIEM) owners.
- IMPORTANT: High-cardinality is mostly a problem for *metrics* (Prometheus/Datadog tags) and some log indexing strategies. For audit logs stored as events and exported to SIEM, cardinality is expected; we just need to constrain/normalize free-form fields and prevent accidental indexing/tagging explosions.

Last updated
- 2026-02-19 (Allison) after initial schema v1 reviews + exporter normalization discussion.

======================================================================
Sheet 1 — Assumptions (inputs)
======================================================================
Assumption key | Value | Notes
---|---|---
A1: Active tenants (Hosted + Dedicated) | 1,200 | internal estimate; long tail is low-volume
A2: “Enterprise/regulated” tenants | 120 | the ones that care most about audit exports + retention
A3: Private deployments (prod) | 45 | mix of VPC + on-prem; growing
A4: Admin active users / tenant (p50/p95) | 6 / 40 | includes SRE/platform operators for Private
A5: Sensitive admin actions / tenant / day (p50/p95) | 25 / 250 | RBAC/key/policy/export/retention changes; excludes read-only views
A6: Auth events (console login, SSO, token issuance) / tenant / day (p50/p95) | 80 / 800 | depends heavily on CI/service accounts
A7: Peak concurrency multiplier | 10x | “all changes during business hours” + batch ops
A8: Avg audit event size (JSON) | 1.4 KB | after redaction + truncation; before compression
A9: Export fanout | 1 target typical | some customers dual-stream (e.g., Splunk + archive)
A10: Ingestion semantics | at-least-once | duplicates possible; SIEM guidance uses event_id for dedupe

Quick derived numbers
- Median tenant: (A5 + A6) = 105 audit events/day
- p95 tenant: (A5 + A6) = 1,050 audit events/day
- Fleet (Hosted+Dedicated) median-ish day: 1,200 * 105 ≈ 126k events/day
- Fleet (Hosted+Dedicated) p95-ish day: 1,200 * 1,050 ≈ 1.26M events/day
- Add Private: 45 * (assume 2,000/day each for operator-heavy envs) ≈ 90k events/day
- Total “plausible high day” ≈ 1.35M events/day
- Data/day (raw JSON): 1.35M * 1.4KB ≈ 1.9 GB/day (pre-compression)

======================================================================
Sheet 2 — Event volume estimates by category (coarse)
======================================================================
Category | Example event_types | Events/tenant/day (p50) | Events/tenant/day (p95) | Notes
---|---|---:|---:|---
RBAC changes | rbac.role.create/update/delete; rbac.binding.update | 2 | 20 | spikes during onboarding or org changes
API key lifecycle | credential.api_key.create/rotate/revoke | 2 | 30 | service accounts can increase volume
Policy/routing changes | policy.routing.update; policy.fallback.update | 1 | 10 | usually rare; can be bursty during incidents
Retention/residency changes | data.retention.update; data.residency.update | <1 | 2 | rare; still must be audited
Audit export config | audit.export.create/update/delete/test | <1 | 5 | spikes during security review/POC
Token issuance/admin auth | auth.token.issue; auth.sso.login | 40 | 400 | includes CI; must constrain user_agent/source_ip handling
Quota overrides/admin ops | gateway.quota.override; gateway.rate_limit.update | 1 | 15 | bursty; often incident-driven
Private installer ops | private.install; private.upgrade; private.rollback; private.config.apply | n/a | n/a | see dedicated Private section below

Private deployment operator note (not per-tenant comparable)
- Private upgrades can emit a fixed set of events per run: install (1), preflight (1), upgrade start (1), component apply (N ~ 10-50), upgrade finish (1), rollback (rare).
- Recommendation: emit one summary event + bounded component list (or separate component events with strict allow-list) to prevent massive payload growth.

======================================================================
Sheet 3 — Cardinality audit: fields (schema v1 candidates)
======================================================================
Legend
- Cardinality risk: LOW / MED / HIGH / EXTREME
- Metrics label allowed?: YES / NO / ONLY-COARSE (only for low-cardinality normalized values)

Field | Example | Cardinality risk | Metrics label allowed? | Constraint / normalization recommendation
---|---|---|---|---
schema_version | "1.0" | LOW | YES | enum; required
occurred_at | ISO8601 timestamp | EXTREME | NO | never as label; used as event timestamp only
event_id | "01HR..." (ULID) | EXTREME | NO | required for dedupe; never as metric label
event_type | "rbac.role.update" | LOW | YES | enum registry (build-time) + reject unknown types
result | "success"/"failure" | LOW | YES | enum
severity | "info"/"warning"/"critical" | LOW | YES | enum; default info
deployment_mode | "hosted"/"dedicated"/"private" | LOW | YES | enum
region | "us-east-1" | LOW | YES | allow-list known regions; "private" -> customer-defined but map to "private" or "private/<cluster_id_hash>" (NOT raw)
service_name | "control-plane" | LOW | YES | allow-list services
environment | "prod"/"staging" | LOW | YES | allow-list
tenant_id | "t_8f3..." | HIGH | ONLY-COARSE | OK in logs; for metrics only in sampled/limited dashboards; avoid global timeseries per tenant by default
project_id | "p_123" | HIGH | NO | log only; for metrics use sampled top-K or hashed bucketing
actor.type | "user"/"service_account"/"system" | LOW | YES | enum
actor.user_id | "u_92ad..." | HIGH | NO | log only; do not index as metric label; SIEM usage ok
actor.email | "alice@company.com" | HIGH (PII) | NO | avoid if possible; if present, store in SIEM but not in Redwood metrics; consider hashed_email for internal correlation
actor.org_role | "owner"/"admin" | LOW | YES | enum; optional
actor.impersonated_by | "u_..." | HIGH | NO | log only; required when impersonation occurs
source.ip | "203.0.113.10" | EXTREME | NO | log only; NEVER metric label; consider /24 bucketing only for internal anomaly metrics (separate pipeline)
source.user_agent | "Mozilla/5.0 ..." | EXTREME | NO | log only; truncate
source.geo | "US" | LOW | YES | optional; coarse geo only if derived internally
request.request_id | uuid | EXTREME | NO | correlation only
request.trace_id | trace id | EXTREME | NO | correlation only
admin_action_id | uuid | EXTREME | NO | correlation only
resource.type | "rbac_role" | LOW | YES | enum registry
resource.id | "role_abc" | HIGH | NO | log only; may be indexed in SIEM but not in Redwood metrics
resource.name | "SRE Admin" | HIGH | NO | avoid; if included, cap length; prefer stable id
changes.before | JSON blob | EXTREME | NO | strongly discourage full before/after; use summarized diffs
changes.after | JSON blob | EXTREME | NO | same as above
changes.diff_summary | "added permission X" | HIGH | NO | recommended: small bounded structured diff fields instead of free-form strings
error.code | "PERMISSION_DENIED" | LOW | YES | enum
error.message | "user not allowed..." | EXTREME | NO | log only; truncate; avoid secrets
siem.target_type | "splunk_hec"/"sentinel" | LOW | YES | exporter only
siem.delivery_status | "delivered"/"retry"/"failed" | LOW | YES | exporter only

Hard rules (should be enforced in library / linting)
- NEVER emit secrets: API keys, tokens, Authorization headers, private keys, signed URLs, KMS material, full request/response bodies.
- NEVER use these as metric labels: event_id, request_id, trace_id, source.ip, source.user_agent, actor.user_id, resource.id, error.message.

======================================================================
Sheet 4 — Proposed allow-lists, truncation, and structured replacements
======================================================================
Area | Risk | Current failure mode | Recommendation
---|---|---|---
user_agent | EXTREME cardinality | dashboards explode if tagged; payload bloat | Store raw UA only in audit event; truncate to 256 chars; do not index in internal telemetry; optionally parse into ua_family/os_family/device_family (LOW cardinality) in separate derived pipeline
IP address | EXTREME cardinality | accidental metric label use; privacy concern | Store full IP only in audit event; never in metrics. If we need anomaly detection metrics: store derived ip_prefix_/24 for IPv4 and /48 for IPv6 (separate pipeline, not customer export by default)
resource.name | HIGH + customer-controlled | role names/policy names unbounded | Cap to 128 chars; prefer stable resource.id + resource.type; do not require name in schema
changes.before/after | payload bloat + accidental PII | someone logs full policy doc or retention config | Replace with: changed_fields (list, max 20), change_count (int), and for select safe fields store old/new values with allow-list (e.g., retention_days: 30->90)
diff_summary (free text) | unbounded strings | high-cardinality + inconsistent semantics | Prefer structured diff schema per event_type. If summary kept, cap to 256 and limit charset (no newlines)
error.message | unbounded strings | can include tokens/ids | error.code required; error.message optional + truncated (256) and scrub patterns
policy identifiers | may be user-provided | label explosion | Use normalized policy_id (UUID) + policy_scope enum (tenant/project). Avoid embedding policy JSON

Suggested safe low-cardinality derived dimensions (for dashboards/alerts)
- event_type
- service_name
- deployment_mode
- region (hosted/dedicated only; private collapsed)
- result
- error.code
- actor.type
- resource.type

======================================================================
Sheet 5 — Ingestion + alerting budget (metrics-oriented)
======================================================================
What we want to alert on (low-cardinality metrics)
Metric | Dimensions (allowed) | Notes
---|---|---
audit_events_emitted_total | service_name, event_type, result, deployment_mode | from producers
audit_events_ingested_total | sink, service_name, deployment_mode | from ingestion pipeline
audit_events_dropped_total | reason, sink, deployment_mode | reason allow-list
audit_delivery_latency_ms (histogram) | deployment_mode, sink | avoid tenant_id dimension
exporter_delivery_attempts_total | target_type, status | exporter only

Proposed internal budgets / guardrails
- Producer-side: no more than ~20 unique metric time series per endpoint per service (rule of thumb) -> achieved by NOT tagging with tenant_id/project_id/user_id.
- Coverage dashboards: compute “expected vs observed event_types” via logs->warehouse query (batch) rather than real-time metrics tagged by tenant.

======================================================================
Sheet 6 — Open questions / TODO
======================================================================
ID | Question | Owner | Status
---|---|---|---
Q1 | Should Private region/cluster be logged as a stable hashed cluster_id vs literal customer cluster name? | Logan Wright | Open
Q2 | For policy changes, do we standardize a structured diff format (changed_fields + values) per policy type? | Jordan Lee | In progress
Q3 | Do we need actor.email in schema v1, or can we rely on actor.user_id + separate lookup? (PII + export expectations) | Naomi Feldman / Olga Petrov | Open
Q4 | Confirm max string lengths (UA, error.message, diff_summary) and enforce in shared library | Sahana Iyer / Kevin Osei | In progress
Q5 | Decide on ULID vs UUIDv7 for event_id (ordering for SIEM + dedupe) | Kevin Osei | In review

======================================================================
Notes / takeaways
======================================================================
- Event volume is not the main risk; unbounded/high-cardinality fields being used as metric labels is the main operational hazard.
- For audit events, we should optimize for: stable enums + correlation IDs + bounded structured diffs. Avoid free-form summaries and full before/after payloads.
- Private deployment needs special attention: installer component-level events can balloon quickly. Prefer summary events with bounded component lists and strict allow-lists.

Change log
- 2026-01-23: initial draft based on schema workshop notes.
- 2026-02-08: added exporter dimensions + at-least-once duplicate note.
- 2026-02-19: added structured diff recommendations and explicit “never as metric label” list.
